# AI Docs — Overview & Shared Contracts

> This is the source of truth for every phase plan in `docs/specs/`. Phase plans implement it; when a phase plan and this document disagree, this document wins and the phase plan must be fixed.

## Goal

A single-page web app (no auth) where a user writes Markdown and an AI co-author proposes edits to the whole document or a selection. Proposals stream in, are shown as a GitHub-style split diff, and the user accepts/rejects each hunk (or all), or refines the proposal with a follow-up instruction. Every accepted AI change is recorded in a version history.

The AI never edits the document directly — every change passes through the user's accept decision.

## Decisions (locked)

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Repo layout | Monorepo, no workspace tooling: `frontend/` (pnpm) and `backend/` (uv). Root `package.json` only hosts Husky. |
| Editor | CodeMirror 6, raw Markdown source, thin React wrapper (no `@uiw/react-codemirror`). |
| Preview | `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm`, styled with `@tailwindcss/typography`. |
| Diff | `diff` (jsdiff) — line diff to build hunks, word diff for intra-line highlight. |
| Review granularity | Per-hunk accept/reject, plus Accept all / Reject all. A decided hunk can be flipped. |
| Transport | `POST /api/suggestions` returns Server-Sent Events. Client reads with `fetch` + `ReadableStream` (not `EventSource`, which cannot POST). |
| AI output format | The model returns **only the replacement text for the target** (selection or whole document). The client computes the diff. No structured edit ops. |
| Refine | A new request carrying the prior turns (`instruction`, `proposal`). Allowed only while no hunk of the current suggestion is accepted. |
| One suggestion at a time | While a suggestion is streaming or under review, new triggers are disabled until it is resolved or discarded. |
| State management | React context + `useReducer`; reducers and helpers are pure and unit-tested. No external state library. |
| Persistence | `localStorage` only, all values Zod-validated on read. |
| Theme | Light by default; toggle to dark; persisted. Tailwind v4 class-based dark variant. |
| LLM providers | Strategy pattern: `anthropic` (default) and `openrouter`, selected by `LLM_PROVIDER`. |
| Models | Logical IDs exposed to UI: `claude-sonnet-5-5` (default), `claude-haiku-5-5`. Each provider maps logical IDs to its own model IDs. |

## Tech stack

Frontend: Node 24, pnpm, React 19, Vite, TypeScript (strict), Tailwind CSS v4 (`@tailwindcss/vite`), Zod v4, Vitest + Testing Library + jsdom, ESLint 9 (flat config) + `eslint-config-prettier`, Prettier, Husky + lint-staged.
Frontend libs: `codemirror`, `@codemirror/lang-markdown`, `@codemirror/language-data`, `@codemirror/theme-one-dark`, `@codemirror/autocomplete` (phase 6), `react-markdown`, `remark-gfm`, `@tailwindcss/typography`, `diff`, `cmdk` (phase 6).

Backend: Python 3.13, uv, FastAPI (`fastapi[standard]`), Pydantic v2 + `pydantic-settings`, `anthropic` SDK, `httpx` (OpenRouter), pytest + `pytest-asyncio`, ruff.

## Phases

| # | Spec | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [01-foundation.md](01-foundation.md) | Git repo, both apps scaffolded, lint/format/test/hooks working, `GET /api/health`, Vite proxy. |
| 2 | [02-editor-core.md](02-editor-core.md) | Usable Markdown editor without AI: tabs (Editor / Preview / AI Review placeholder), CodeMirror editor, preview, localStorage autosave, export `.md`, light/dark theme. |
| 3 | [03-backend-ai.md](03-backend-ai.md) | LLM provider strategy, `GET /api/models`, streaming `POST /api/suggestions` (SSE). Fully tested with a fake provider. |
| 4 | [04-ai-suggestions.md](04-ai-suggestions.md) | Model dropdown, "Ask AI" bar, streaming proposal, split diff review with per-hunk accept/reject, refine, stale detection. |
| 5 | [05-version-history.md](05-version-history.md) | Version timeline in the AI Review tab, diff between versions, restore, manual snapshots. |
| 6 | [06-commands-and-polish.md](06-commands-and-polish.md) | AI presets, command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K), slash commands in the editor, keyboard shortcuts, README. |

Each phase ends with working, tested software. Phases 2 and 3 are independent of each other; 4 needs 2 and 3; 5 needs 4; 6 needs 4 (and uses 5's tab layout).

## Architecture

```
Browser (React SPA, :5173)                         FastAPI (:8000)
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ Header: ModelSelect · ThemeToggle ·     │        │ GET  /api/health             │
│         ExportButton                    │  /api  │ GET  /api/models             │
│ Tabs:  Editor | Preview | AI Review     │──────▶ │ POST /api/suggestions (SSE)  │
│                                         │ (Vite  │        │                     │
│ DocumentProvider  (content, selection)  │ proxy) │  build_completion_request    │
│ SuggestionProvider (active suggestion)  │        │        │                     │
│ VersionsProvider  (history)             │        │  LLMProvider (strategy)      │
│ ModelProvider     (catalog, selected)   │        │   ├─ AnthropicProvider       │
│ ThemeProvider                           │        │   └─ OpenRouterProvider      │
│ localStorage ◀── persistence            │        └──────────────────────────────┘
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Suggestion lifecycle:

1. User triggers (button / palette / slash) with an instruction and a target (`auto` = selection if non-empty, else document).
2. Client records `baseText` (the target's current text) and the scope, then POSTs to `/api/suggestions`.
3. `delta` events append to `proposedText` (shown live in the AI Review tab, which opens automatically).
4. On `done`, the client normalizes the proposal and computes diff segments → status `reviewing`.
5. Each accept/reject recomputes the region text from the segments, locates the region in the current document, and replaces it. If the region can't be located → `stale` (user can only discard).
6. When no hunk is `pending`, the suggestion is resolved. If any hunk was accepted, `onResolved` fires (phase 5 records versions), and the active suggestion is cleared.

## Backend contract

### Configuration (env, via `pydantic-settings`, `.env` supported)

| Var | Type / default | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | JSON list of str, default `["http://localhost:5173"]` | 1 |
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `"anthropic"` \| `"openrouter"`, default `"anthropic"` | 3 |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | str \| None | 3 |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | str \| None | 3 |
| `LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL` | str, default `"claude-sonnet-5-5"` (must be a catalog ID) | 3 |
| `LLM_EFFORT` | `"low"` \| `"medium"` \| `"high"`, default `"low"` (Anthropic `output_config.effort`; interactive latency matters) | 3 |
| `LLM_MAX_TOKENS` | int, default `64000` | 3 |

### Endpoints

`GET /api/health` → `200 {"status": "ok"}`

`GET /api/models` →
```json
{
  "provider": "anthropic",
  "default_model": "claude-sonnet-5-5",
  "models": [
    {"id": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "label": "Claude Sonnet 5.5"},
    {"id": "claude-haiku-5-5", "label": "Claude Haiku 5.5"}
  ]
}
```

`POST /api/suggestions` — request body:
```json
{
  "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5",
  "document": "# Title\n\nFull markdown…",
  "selection": {"start": 10, "end": 42},
  "instruction": "Make this more concise",
  "history": [{"instruction": "Rewrite formally", "proposal": "…previous proposal…"}]
}
```
- `selection`: `null` → whole document is the target. Offsets are UTF-16 code-unit offsets into `document` (what JS `String` uses); `0 <= start < end <= len(document)` measured in UTF-16 units. The backend slices using a UTF-16-safe helper.
- `instruction`: 1–2000 chars after strip. `document`: max 200 000 chars. `history`: max 10 turns.
- Validation errors → `422` (FastAPI default). Unknown `model` → `422` with `{"detail": "Unknown model: <id>"}`. Both happen **before** streaming starts.

Response: `200`, `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, headers `Cache-Control: no-cache`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. Events (each `data` is one JSON line):
```
event: delta
data: {"text": "partial text"}

event: done
data: {"stop_reason": "end_turn"}

event: error
data: {"code": "rate_limited", "message": "Human-readable message"}
```
Exactly one terminal event (`done` or `error`) ends every stream. Error codes: `auth_error`, `rate_limited`, `provider_unavailable`, `refused`, `bad_request`, `internal_error`. On `error`, the client discards any streamed text.

### Prompt contract (phase 3, `app/suggestions/prompt.py`)

- System prompt: the model is a co-author editing a Markdown document; it outputs **only** the rewritten target text — no preamble, no explanation, no code fences around the output; it makes the minimal changes needed to satisfy the instruction and preserves everything else verbatim (including Markdown syntax and trailing newline).
- First user message: the full document in `<document>…</document>`. With a selection, the target is marked inline with `<target>` / `</target>` tags inside the document, plus the target repeated in `<target_text>…</target_text>`. Then `<instruction>…</instruction>`, and a closing line: rewrite only the target (or the whole document when there is no selection).
- Refine history: for each turn in `history`, the first user message uses that turn's instruction, followed by `assistant: <proposal>`, then `user: Refine your previous rewrite: <next instruction>`. The final message is always `user` (no assistant prefill).

### Python interfaces

```python
# app/llm/types.py
Role = Literal["user", "assistant"]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChatMessage:
    role: Role
    content: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CompletionRequest:
    model: str            # logical catalog ID, e.g. "claude-sonnet-5-5"
    system: str
    messages: list[ChatMessage]
    max_tokens: int

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TextDelta:
    text: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StreamDone:
    stop_reason: str

StreamEvent = TextDelta | StreamDone

ErrorCode = Literal["auth_error", "rate_limited", "provider_unavailable", "refused", "bad_request", "internal_error"]

class ProviderError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code: ErrorCode, message: str) -> None: ...
    code: ErrorCode
    message: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)

    id: str

# app/llm/catalog.py
MODELS: tuple[ModelInfo, ...]  # sonnet 5.5 first, haiku 5.5 second

# app/llm/base.py
class LLMProvider(Protocol):
    name: str
    def stream(self, request: CompletionRequest) -> AsyncIterator[StreamEvent]: ...
    # Yields TextDelta* then exactly one StreamDone, or raises ProviderError.

# app/llm/factory.py
def build_provider(settings: Settings) -> LLMProvider: ...
def get_provider() -> LLMProvider: ...   # FastAPI dependency; cached per process

# app/suggestions/schemas.py  (Pydantic)
class Selection(BaseModel): start: int; end: int
class RefineTurn(BaseModel): instruction: str; proposal: str
class SuggestionRequest(BaseModel):
    model: str; document: str; selection: Selection | None = None
    instruction: str; history: list[RefineTurn] = []

# app/suggestions/prompt.py
SYSTEM_PROMPT: str

def build_completion_request(req: SuggestionRequest, max_tokens: int) -> CompletionRequest: ...

# app/suggestions/sse.py
def format_sse(event: str, data: dict[str, object]) -> str: ...  # "event: x\ndata: {json}\n\n"

Provider model mapping: Anthropic uses the logical ID as-is (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5`). OpenRouter maps to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` and `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` — **verify these slugs on openrouter.ai/models during phase 3** and update the constant if they differ.

Anthropic specifics: `AsyncAnthropic().beta.messages.stream(...)` with `output_config={"effort": LLM_EFFORT}`. Adaptive thinking is the default on both models (omit `thinking`); thinking display is omitted by default, so `text_stream` carries only answer text. For `claude-sonnet-5-5` add server-side refusal fallback: `betas=["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"], fallbacks="default"` (not supported for Haiku 5.5). After the stream, `stop_reason == "refusal"` → `ProviderError("refused", …)`. Map SDK errors most-specific-first: `AuthenticationError`/`PermissionDeniedError` → `auth_error`, `RateLimitError` → `rate_limited`, `BadRequestError` → `bad_request`, other `APIStatusError` → `provider_unavailable`, `APIConnectionError` → `provider_unavailable`.

# AI Docs — Overview & Shared Contracts

> This is the source of truth for every phase plan in `docs/specs/`. Phase plans implement it; when a phase plan and this document disagree, this document wins and the phase plan must be fixed.

## Goal

A single-page web app (no auth) where a user writes Markdown and an AI co-author proposes edits to the whole document or a selection. Proposals stream in, are shown as a GitHub-style split diff, and the user accepts/rejects each hunk (or all), or refines the proposal with a follow-up instruction. Every accepted AI change is recorded in a version history.

The AI never edits the document directly — every change passes through the user's accept decision.

## Decisions (locked)

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Repo layout | Monorepo, no workspace tooling: `frontend/` (pnpm) and `backend/` (uv). Root `package.json` only hosts Husky. |
| Editor | CodeMirror 6, raw Markdown source, thin React wrapper (no `@uiw/react-codemirror`). |
| Preview | `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm`, styled with `@tailwindcss/typography`. |
| Diff | `diff` (jsdiff) — line diff to build hunks, word diff for intra-line highlight. |
| Review granularity | Per-hunk accept/reject, plus Accept all / Reject all. A decided hunk can be flipped. |
| Transport | `POST /api/suggestions` returns Server-Sent Events. Client reads with `fetch` + `ReadableStream` (not `EventSource`, which cannot POST). |
| AI output format | The model returns **only the replacement text for the target** (selection or whole document). The client computes the diff. No structured edit ops. |
| Refine | A new request carrying the prior turns (`instruction`, `proposal`). Allowed only while no hunk of the current suggestion is accepted. |
| One suggestion at a time | While a suggestion is streaming or under review, new triggers are disabled until it is resolved or discarded. |
| State management | React context + `useReducer`; reducers and helpers are pure and unit-tested. No external state library. |
| Persistence | `localStorage` only, all values Zod-validated on read. |
| Theme | Light by default; toggle to dark; persisted. Tailwind v4 class-based dark variant. |
| LLM providers | Strategy pattern: `anthropic` (default) and `openrouter`, selected by `LLM_PROVIDER`. |
| Models | Logical IDs exposed to UI: `claude-sonnet-5-5` (default), `claude-haiku-5-5`. Each provider maps logical IDs to its own model IDs. |

## Tech stack

Frontend: Node 24, pnpm, React 19, Vite, TypeScript (strict), Tailwind CSS v4 (`@tailwindcss/vite`), Zod v4, Vitest + Testing Library + jsdom, ESLint 9 (flat config) + `eslint-config-prettier`, Prettier, Husky + lint-staged.
Frontend libs: `codemirror`, `@codemirror/lang-markdown`, `@codemirror/language-data`, `@codemirror/theme-one-dark`, `@codemirror/autocomplete` (phase 6), `react-markdown`, `remark-gfm`, `@tailwindcss/typography`, `diff`, `cmdk` (phase 6).

Backend: Python 3.13, uv, FastAPI (`fastapi[standard]`), Pydantic v2 + `pydantic-settings`, `anthropic` SDK, `httpx` (OpenRouter), pytest + `pytest-asyncio`, ruff.

## Phases

| # | Spec | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [01-foundation.md](01-foundation.md) | Git repo, both apps scaffolded, lint/format/test/hooks working, `GET /api/health`, Vite proxy. |
| 2 | [02-editor-core.md](02-editor-core.md) | Usable Markdown editor without AI: tabs (Editor / Preview / AI Review placeholder), CodeMirror editor, preview, localStorage autosave, export `.md`, light/dark theme. |
| 3 | [03-backend-ai.md](03-backend-ai.md) | LLM provider strategy, `GET /api/models`, streaming `POST /api/suggestions` (SSE). Fully tested with a fake provider. |
| 4 | [04-ai-suggestions.md](04-ai-suggestions.md) | Model dropdown, "Ask AI" bar, streaming proposal, split diff review with per-hunk accept/reject, refine, stale detection. |
| 5 | [05-version-history.md](05-version-history.md) | Version timeline in the AI Review tab, diff between versions, restore, manual snapshots. |
| 6 | [06-commands-and-polish.md](06-commands-and-polish.md) | AI presets, command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K), slash commands in the editor, keyboard shortcuts, README. |

Each phase ends with working, tested software. Phases 2 and 3 are independent of each other; 4 needs 2 and 3; 5 needs 4; 6 needs 4 (and uses 5's tab layout).

## Architecture

```
Browser (React SPA, :5173)                         FastAPI (:8000)
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ Header: ModelSelect · ThemeToggle ·     │        │ GET  /api/health             │
│         ExportButton                    │  /api  │ GET  /api/models             │
│ Tabs:  Editor | Preview | AI Review     │──────▶ │ POST /api/suggestions (SSE)  │
│                                         │ (Vite  │        │                     │
│ DocumentProvider  (content, selection)  │ proxy) │  build_completion_request    │
│ SuggestionProvider (active suggestion)  │        │        │                     │
│ VersionsProvider  (history)             │        │  LLMProvider (strategy)      │
│ ModelProvider     (catalog, selected)   │        │   ├─ AnthropicProvider       │
│ ThemeProvider                           │        │   └─ OpenRouterProvider      │
│ localStorage ◀── persistence            │        └──────────────────────────────┘
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Suggestion lifecycle:

1. User triggers (button / palette / slash) with an instruction and a target (`auto` = selection if non-empty, else document).
2. Client records `baseText` (the target's current text) and the scope, then POSTs to `/api/suggestions`.
3. `delta` events append to `proposedText` (shown live in the AI Review tab, which opens automatically).
4. On `done`, the client normalizes the proposal and computes diff segments → status `reviewing`.
5. Each accept/reject recomputes the region text from the segments, locates the region in the current document, and replaces it. If the region can't be located → `stale` (user can only discard).
6. When no hunk is `pending`, the suggestion is resolved. If any hunk was accepted, `onResolved` fires (phase 5 records versions), and the active suggestion is cleared.

## Backend contract

### Configuration (env, via `pydantic-settings`, `.env` supported)

| Var | Type / default | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | JSON list of str, default `["http://localhost:5173"]` | 1 |
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `"anthropic"` \| `"openrouter"`, default `"anthropic"` | 3 |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | str \| None | 3 |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | str \| None | 3 |
| `LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL` | str, default `"claude-sonnet-5-5"` (must be a catalog ID) | 3 |
| `LLM_EFFORT` | `"low"` \| `"medium"` \| `"high"`, default `"low"` (Anthropic `output_config.effort`; interactive latency matters) | 3 |
| `LLM_MAX_TOKENS` | int, default `64000` | 3 |

### Endpoints

`GET /api/health` → `200 {"status": "ok"}`

`GET /api/models` →
```json
{
  "provider": "anthropic",
  "default_model": "claude-sonnet-5-5",
  "models": [
    {"id": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "label": "Claude Sonnet 5.5"},
    {"id": "claude-haiku-5-5", "label": "Claude Haiku 5.5"}
  ]
}
```

`POST /api/suggestions` — request body:
```json
{
  "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5",
  "document": "# Title\n\nFull markdown…",
  "selection": {"start": 10, "end": 42},
  "instruction": "Make this more concise",
  "history": [{"instruction": "Rewrite formally", "proposal": "…previous proposal…"}]
}
```
- `selection`: `null` → whole document is the target. Offsets are UTF-16 code-unit offsets into `document` (what JS `String` uses); `0 <= start < end <= len(document)` measured in UTF-16 units. The backend slices using a UTF-16-safe helper.
- `instruction`: 1–2000 chars after strip. `document`: max 200 000 chars. `history`: max 10 turns.
- Validation errors → `422` (FastAPI default). Unknown `model` → `422` with `{"detail": "Unknown model: <id>"}`. Both happen **before** streaming starts.

Response: `200`, `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, headers `Cache-Control: no-cache`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. Events (each `data` is one JSON line):
```
event: delta
data: {"text": "partial text"}

event: done
data: {"stop_reason": "end_turn"}

event: error
data: {"code": "rate_limited", "message": "Human-readable message"}
```
Exactly one terminal event (`done` or `error`) ends every stream. Error codes: `auth_error`, `rate_limited`, `provider_unavailable`, `refused`, `bad_request`, `internal_error`. On `error`, the client discards any streamed text.

### Prompt contract (phase 3, `app/suggestions/prompt.py`)

- System prompt: the model is a co-author editing a Markdown document; it outputs **only** the rewritten target text — no preamble, no explanation, no code fences around the output; it makes the minimal changes needed to satisfy the instruction and preserves everything else verbatim (including Markdown syntax and trailing newline).
- First user message: the full document in `<document>…</document>`. With a selection, the target is marked inline with `<target>` / `</target>` tags inside the document, plus the target repeated in `<target_text>…</target_text>`. Then `<instruction>…</instruction>`, and a closing line: rewrite only the target (or the whole document when there is no selection).
- Refine history: for each turn in `history`, the first user message uses that turn's instruction, followed by `assistant: <proposal>`, then `user: Refine your previous rewrite: <next instruction>`. The final message is always `user` (no assistant prefill).

### Python interfaces

```python

Role = Literal["user", "assistant"]

@dataclass(frozen=True)

    role: Role

@dataclass(frozen=True)

    def __init__(self, code: ErrorCode, message: str) -> None: ...
    code: ErrorCode
    message: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)

    id: str
    label: str

MODELS: tuple[ModelInfo, ...]  # sonnet 5.5 first, haiku 5.5 second

    name: str
    def stream(self, request: CompletionRequest) -> AsyncIterator[StreamEvent]: ...
    # Yields TextDelta* then exactly one StreamDone, or raises ProviderError.

# app/llm/factory.py

    model: str; document: str; selection: Selection | None = None
    instruction: str; history: list[RefineTurn] = []

# app/suggestions/prompt.py
SYSTEM_PROMPT: str

def build_completion_request(req: SuggestionRequest, max_tokens: int) -> CompletionRequest: ...

Provider model mapping: Anthropic uses the logical ID as-is (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5`). OpenRouter maps to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` and `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` — **verify these slugs on openrouter.ai/models during phase 3** and update the constant if they differ.

Anthropic specifics: `AsyncAnthropic().beta.messages.stream(...)` with `output_config={"effort": LLM_EFFORT}`. Adaptive thinking is the default on both models (omit `thinking`); thinking display is omitted by default, so `text_stream` carries only answer text. For `claude-sonnet-5-5` add server-side refusal fallback: `betas=["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"], fallbacks="default"` (not supported for Haiku 5.5). After the stream, `stop_reason == "refusal"` → `ProviderError("refused", …)`. Map SDK errors most-specific-first: `AuthenticationError`/`PermissionDeniedError` → `auth_error`, `RateLimitError` → `rate_limited`, `BadRequestError` → `bad_request`, other `APIStatusError` → `provider_unavailable`, `APIConnectionError` → `provider_unavailable`.

# AI Docs — Overview & Shared Contracts

> This is the source of truth for every phase plan in `docs/specs/`. Phase plans implement it; when a phase plan and this document disagree, this document wins and the phase plan must be fixed.

## Goal

A single-page web app (no auth) where a user writes Markdown and an AI co-author proposes edits to the whole document or a selection. Proposals stream in, are shown as a GitHub-style split diff, and the user accepts/rejects each hunk (or all), or refines the proposal with a follow-up instruction. Every accepted AI change is recorded in a version history.

The AI never edits the document directly — every change passes through the user's accept decision.

## Decisions (locked)

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Repo layout | Monorepo, no workspace tooling: `frontend/` (pnpm) and `backend/` (uv). Root `package.json` only hosts Husky. |
| Editor | CodeMirror 6, raw Markdown source, thin React wrapper (no `@uiw/react-codemirror`). |
| Preview | `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm`, styled with `@tailwindcss/typography`. |
| Diff | `diff` (jsdiff) — line diff to build hunks, word diff for intra-line highlight. |
| Review granularity | Per-hunk accept/reject, plus Accept all / Reject all. A decided hunk can be flipped. |
| Transport | `POST /api/suggestions` returns Server-Sent Events. Client reads with `fetch` + `ReadableStream` (not `EventSource`, which cannot POST). |
| AI output format | The model returns **only the replacement text for the target** (selection or whole document). The client computes the diff. No structured edit ops. |
| Refine | A new request carrying the prior turns (`instruction`, `proposal`). Allowed only while no hunk of the current suggestion is accepted. |
| One suggestion at a time | While a suggestion is streaming or under review, new triggers are disabled until it is resolved or discarded. |
| State management | React context + `useReducer`; reducers and helpers are pure and unit-tested. No external state library. |
| Persistence | `localStorage` only, all values Zod-validated on read. |
| Theme | Light by default; toggle to dark; persisted. Tailwind v4 class-based dark variant. |
| LLM providers | Strategy pattern: `anthropic` (default) and `openrouter`, selected by `LLM_PROVIDER`. |
| Models | Logical IDs exposed to UI: `claude-sonnet-5-5` (default), `claude-haiku-5-5`. Each provider maps logical IDs to its own model IDs. |

## Tech stack

Frontend: Node 24, pnpm, React 19, Vite, TypeScript (strict), Tailwind CSS v4 (`@tailwindcss/vite`), Zod v4, Vitest + Testing Library + jsdom, ESLint 9 (flat config) + `eslint-config-prettier`, Prettier, Husky + lint-staged.
Frontend libs: `codemirror`, `@codemirror/lang-markdown`, `@codemirror/language-data`, `@codemirror/theme-one-dark`, `@codemirror/autocomplete` (phase 6), `react-markdown`, `remark-gfm`, `@tailwindcss/typography`, `diff`, `cmdk` (phase 6).

Backend: Python 3.13, uv, FastAPI (`fastapi[standard]`), Pydantic v2 + `pydantic-settings`, `anthropic` SDK, `httpx` (OpenRouter), pytest + `pytest-asyncio`, ruff.

## Phases

| # | Spec | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [01-foundation.md](01-foundation.md) | Git repo, both apps scaffolded, lint/format/test/hooks working, `GET /api/health`, Vite proxy. |
| 2 | [02-editor-core.md](02-editor-core.md) | Usable Markdown editor without AI: tabs (Editor / Preview / AI Review placeholder), CodeMirror editor, preview, localStorage autosave, export `.md`, light/dark theme. |
| 3 | [03-backend-ai.md](03-backend-ai.md) | LLM provider strategy, `GET /api/models`, streaming `POST /api/suggestions` (SSE). Fully tested with a fake provider. |
| 4 | [04-ai-suggestions.md](04-ai-suggestions.md) | Model dropdown, "Ask AI" bar, streaming proposal, split diff review with per-hunk accept/reject, refine, stale detection. |
| 5 | [05-version-history.md](05-version-history.md) | Version timeline in the AI Review tab, diff between versions, restore, manual snapshots. |
| 6 | [06-commands-and-polish.md](06-commands-and-polish.md) | AI presets, command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K), slash commands in the editor, keyboard shortcuts, README. |

Each phase ends with working, tested software. Phases 2 and 3 are independent of each other; 4 needs 2 and 3; 5 needs 4; 6 needs 4 (and uses 5's tab layout).

## Architecture

```
Browser (React SPA, :5173)                         FastAPI (:8000)
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ Header: ModelSelect · ThemeToggle ·     │        │ GET  /api/health             │
│         ExportButton                    │  /api  │ GET  /api/models             │
│ Tabs:  Editor | Preview | AI Review     │──────▶ │ POST /api/suggestions (SSE)  │
│                                         │ (Vite  │        │                     │
│ DocumentProvider  (content, selection)  │ proxy) │  build_completion_request    │
│ SuggestionProvider (active suggestion)  │        │        │                     │
│ VersionsProvider  (history)             │        │  LLMProvider (strategy)      │
│ ModelProvider     (catalog, selected)   │        │   ├─ AnthropicProvider       │
│ ThemeProvider                           │        │   └─ OpenRouterProvider      │
│ localStorage ◀── persistence            │        └──────────────────────────────┘
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Suggestion lifecycle:

1. User triggers (button / palette / slash) with an instruction and a target (`auto` = selection if non-empty, else document).
2. Client records `baseText` (the target's current text) and the scope, then POSTs to `/api/suggestions`.
3. `delta` events append to `proposedText` (shown live in the AI Review tab, which opens automatically).
4. On `done`, the client normalizes the proposal and computes diff segments → status `reviewing`.
5. Each accept/reject recomputes the region text from the segments, locates the region in the current document, and replaces it. If the region can't be located → `stale` (user can only discard).
6. When no hunk is `pending`, the suggestion is resolved. If any hunk was accepted, `onResolved` fires (phase 5 records versions), and the active suggestion is cleared.

## Backend contract

### Configuration (env, via `pydantic-settings`, `.env` supported)

| Var | Type / default | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | JSON list of str, default `["http://localhost:5173"]` | 1 |
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `"anthropic"` \| `"openrouter"`, default `"anthropic"` | 3 |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | str \| None | 3 |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | str \| None | 3 |
| `LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL` | str, default `"claude-sonnet-5-5"` (must be a catalog ID) | 3 |
| `LLM_EFFORT` | `"low"` \| `"medium"` \| `"high"`, default `"low"` (Anthropic `output_config.effort`; interactive latency matters) | 3 |
| `LLM_MAX_TOKENS` | int, default `64000` | 3 |

### Endpoints

`GET /api/health` → `200 {"status": "ok"}`

`GET /api/models` →
```json
{
  "provider": "anthropic",
  "default_model": "claude-sonnet-5-5",
  "models": [
    {"id": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "label": "Claude Sonnet 5.5"},
    {"id": "claude-haiku-5-5", "label": "Claude Haiku 5.5"}
  ]
}
```

`POST /api/suggestions` — request body:
```json
{
  "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5",
  "document": "# Title\n\nFull markdown…",
  "selection": {"start": 10, "end": 42},
  "instruction": "Make this more concise",
  "history": [{"instruction": "Rewrite formally", "proposal": "…previous proposal…"}]
}
```
- `selection`: `null` → whole document is the target. Offsets are UTF-16 code-unit offsets into `document` (what JS `String` uses); `0 <= start < end <= len(document)` measured in UTF-16 units. The backend slices using a UTF-16-safe helper.
- `instruction`: 1–2000 chars after strip. `document`: max 200 000 chars. `history`: max 10 turns.
- Validation errors → `422` (FastAPI default). Unknown `model` → `422` with `{"detail": "Unknown model: <id>"}`. Both happen **before** streaming starts.

Response: `200`, `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, headers `Cache-Control: no-cache`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. Events (each `data` is one JSON line):
```
event: delta
data: {"text": "partial text"}

event: done
data: {"stop_reason": "end_turn"}

event: error
data: {"code": "rate_limited", "message": "Human-readable message"}
```
Exactly one terminal event (`done` or `error`) ends every stream. Error codes: `auth_error`, `rate_limited`, `provider_unavailable`, `refused`, `bad_request`, `internal_error`. On `error`, the client discards any streamed text.

### Prompt contract (phase 3, `app/suggestions/prompt.py`)

- System prompt: the model is a co-author editing a Markdown document; it outputs **only** the rewritten target text — no preamble, no explanation, no code fences around the output; it makes the minimal changes needed to satisfy the instruction and preserves everything else verbatim (including Markdown syntax and trailing newline).
- First user message: the full document in `<document>…</document>`. With a selection, the target is marked inline with `<target>` / `</target>` tags inside the document, plus the target repeated in `<target_text>…</target_text>`. Then `<instruction>…</instruction>`, and a closing line: rewrite only the target (or the whole document when there is no selection).
- Refine history: for each turn in `history`, the first user message uses that turn's instruction, followed by `assistant: <proposal>`, then `user: Refine your previous rewrite: <next instruction>`. The final message is always `user` (no assistant prefill).

### Python interfaces

```python
# app/llm/types.py
Role = Literal["user", "assistant"]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChatMessage:
    role: Role
    content: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CompletionRequest:
    model: str            # logical catalog ID, e.g. "claude-sonnet-5-5"
    system: str
    messages: list[ChatMessage]
    max_tokens: int

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TextDelta:
    text: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StreamDone:
    stop_reason: str

StreamEvent = TextDelta | StreamDone

ErrorCode = Literal["auth_error", "rate_limited", "provider_unavailable", "refused", "bad_request", "internal_error"]

class ProviderError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code: ErrorCode, message: str) -> None: ...
    code: ErrorCode
    message: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModelInfo:
    id: str
    label: str

# app/llm/catalog.py
MODELS: tuple[ModelInfo, ...]  # sonnet 5.5 first, haiku 5.5 second
def get_model(model_id: str) -> ModelInfo | None: ...

# app/llm/base.py
class LLMProvider(Protocol):
    name: str
    def stream(self, request: CompletionRequest) -> AsyncIterator[StreamEvent]: ...
    # Yields TextDelta* then exactly one StreamDone, or raises ProviderError.

# app/llm/factory.py
def build_provider(settings: Settings) -> LLMProvider: ...
def get_provider() -> LLMProvider: ...   # FastAPI dependency; cached per process

# app/suggestions/schemas.py  (Pydantic)
class Selection(BaseModel): start: int; end: int
class RefineTurn(BaseModel): instruction: str; proposal: str
class SuggestionRequest(BaseModel):
    model: str; document: str; selection: Selection | None = None
    instruction: str; history: list[RefineTurn] = []

# app/suggestions/prompt.py
SYSTEM_PROMPT: str
def utf16_slice(text: str, start: int, end: int) -> str: ...
def build_completion_request(req: SuggestionRequest, max_tokens: int) -> CompletionRequest: ...

# app/suggestions/sse.py
def format_sse(event: str, data: dict[str, object]) -> str: ...  # "event: x\ndata: {json}\n\n"
```

Provider model mapping: Anthropic uses the logical ID as-is (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5`). OpenRouter maps to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` and `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` — **verify these slugs on openrouter.ai/models during phase 3** and update the constant if they differ.

Anthropic specifics: `AsyncAnthropic().beta.messages.stream(...)` with `output_config={"effort": LLM_EFFORT}`. Adaptive thinking is the default on both models (omit `thinking`); thinking display is omitted by default, so `text_stream` carries only answer text. For `claude-sonnet-5-5` add server-side refusal fallback: `betas=["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"], fallbacks="default"` (not supported for Haiku 5.5). After the stream, `stop_reason == "refusal"` → `ProviderError("refused", …)`. Map SDK errors most-specific-first: `AuthenticationError`/`PermissionDeniedError` → `auth_error`, `RateLimitError` → `rate_limited`, `BadRequestError` → `bad_request`, other `APIStatusError` → `provider_unavailable`, `APIConnectionError` → `provider_unavailable`.

<result>I wrote the phase 5 plan to /Users/buemura/dev/projects/ai-docs/docs/specs/05-version-history.md. I didn't commit it.

It has 7 tasks, each test-first with full code:
1. Version schema and the pure history reducer.
2. The history store: saving and loading, the first version, and restore.
3. Recording a version when an AI suggestion is finished.
4. A relative-time helper and the version list.
5. The read-only diff against the previous version, with "Restore this version".
6. The history section with the "Save snapshot" button.
7. The AI Review tab, the final wiring in `App.tsx`, and an app-level test.

**Assumptions about phase 4.** These are listed in a pre-flight section of grep commands that confirm each one exists:
- The document store (`DocumentProvider`) loads the saved document on its first render, not afterwards. Task 2's first test catches this, and the plan says how to fix the store if not.
- `SplitDiffView` is a named export that takes `{ segments, readOnly? }`, and its accept/reject callbacks are optional when `readOnly` is set. This is the only part not in the overview: it doesn't define those props, so phase 4 needs to match.
- `SuggestionPanel` takes no props and shows its own empty state.
- `useModels` is exported from `features/ai/ModelProvider.tsx`.
- `App.tsx` default-exports `App`, which holds the tab state, wraps `AppShell` in `SuggestionProvider` with `onStart`, and has `review: <SuggestionPanel />`.

**Changes beyond the overview:**
- Three new files in `features/history/`: `SuggestionBridge.tsx`, `relativeTime.ts` and `VersionHistory.tsx`.
- Two extra constants: `QUOTA_FALLBACK_KEEP = 20` and `VERSIONS_STORAGE_KEY`.
- A `VersionInput` type, used as the argument to `record`.

**Design choices worth knowing:**
- The first version is created when the history store is first set up, not in a later effect. That avoids the double run in React's StrictMode.
- If saving fails because storage is full, it saves only the newest 20 versions and tries once. The full list stays in memory for the current session.
- If the document has been edited by hand since the last version, the AI handler first records a "Manual edits" version, so the diff for the AI version stays clean.

The app-level test is in a new file, `src/App.history.test.tsx`, so it doesn't overwrite any earlier App tests.</result>

**Task count:** 11 tasks:
1. Types and diff engine
2. normalize, locateRegion and resolveTarget
3. Schemas, SSE parser, test helpers and a default fetch stub
4. API client
5. ModelProvider, ModelSelect and header wiring
6. Reducer
7. SuggestionProvider
8. SplitDiffView
9. AskAiBar
10. SuggestionPanel
11. App wiring, integration test and the manual end-to-end check

**Aligned to the phase 2 plan as written:**
- `TextRange` is imported from `features/document/schema.ts`.
- `ModelSelect` goes into the `AppHeader` children slot.
- Colours use the slate palette, and colocated hooks get the same eslint-disable comment phase 2 uses.
- `App` stays a default export with an `AppShell`.
- Task 11 replaces phase 2's "AI suggestions will appear here." test in `App.test.tsx`, because the empty review panel changes that text.

**Additions to the overview contract** (phases 5 and 6 may want them listed in the overview):
- `useSuggestion().retry()`. The Retry button can't run `discard()` then `start()` in one handler, because `start` would still see the old suggestion and refuse.
- `discard()` calls `onResolved` when hunks were already accepted, so version history doesn't miss partly reviewed suggestions. The overview only fires it when nothing is left pending.
- Extra exports:
  - `getHunks`, `setHunkStatuses`, `splitLines` and `countLines` from `diff.ts`
  - `resolveTarget` from `locateRegion.ts`
  - `MODEL_STORAGE_KEY` from `ModelProvider.tsx`
  - `SplitDiffView` takes a `contextLines` prop
- Test helpers in `src/test/sse.ts` and `src/test/renderWithAi.tsx`.
- `src/test/setup.ts` now makes `fetch` reject in every test unless the test mocks it, and resets the stub afterwards. I checked phase 2's setup: its CodeMirror polyfills don't stub globals, so this won't undo them.

**Assumptions:**
- Refine and retry send the current document and find the original target text again. If it can't be found, the suggestion is marked stale (refine) or shows a "target changed" error (retry).
- A collapsed or empty range falls back to the whole document.
- If the user typed text after a whole-document target, the accept still applies and the extra text is kept.
- Hunk IDs are `hunk-1`, `hunk-2`, … for each suggestion.
- Making the final decision on the last pending hunk resolves the suggestion at once, so those decisions can't be revisited.
- The review tab badge shows `…` while streaming, then the number of pending hunks.</result>

**Aligned to the phase 2 plan as written:**
- `TextRange` is imported from `features/document/schema.ts`.

**Additions to the overview contract** (phases 5 and 6 may want them listed in the overview):
- `useSuggestion().retry()`. The Retry button can't run `discard()` then `start()` in one handler, because `start` would still see the old suggestion and refuse.
- `discard()` calls `onResolved` when hunks were already accepted, so version history doesn't miss partly reviewed suggestions. The overview only fires it when nothing is left pending.
- Extra exports:
  - `getHunks`, `setHunkStatuses`, `splitLines` and `countLines` from `diff.ts`
  - `resolveTarget` from `locateRegion.ts`
  - `MODEL_STORAGE_KEY` from `ModelProvider.tsx`
  - `SplitDiffView` takes a `contextLines` prop
- Test helpers in `src/test/sse.ts` and `src/test/renderWithAi.tsx`.
- `src/test/setup.ts` now makes `fetch` reject in every test unless the test mocks it, and resets the stub afterwards. I checked phase 2's setup: its CodeMirror polyfills don't stub globals, so this won't undo them.

**Assumptions:**
- Refine and retry send the current document and find the original target text again. If it can't be found, the suggestion is marked stale (refine) or shows a "target changed" error (retry).
- A collapsed or empty range falls back to the whole document.
- If the user typed text after a whole-document target, the accept still applies and the extra text is kept.
- Hunk IDs are `hunk-1`, `hunk-2`, … for each suggestion.
- Making the final decision on the last pending hunk resolves the suggestion at once, so those decisions can't be revisited.
- The review tab badge shows `…` while streaming, then the number of pending hunks.</result>

Load plan, review critically, execute all tasks, report when complete.

2. Read plan file
3. Review critically - identify any questions or concerns about the plan
4. If concerns: Raise them with your human partner before starting

### Step 2: Execute Tasks

For each task:
1. Mark as in_progress
2. Follow each step exactly (plan has bite-sized steps)
3. Run verifications as specified
4. Mark as completed

- Announce: "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch

## When to Stop and Ask for Help

**STOP executing immediately when:**
- Hit a blocker (missing dependency, test fails, instruction unclear)
- Plan has critical gaps preventing starting
- You don't understand an instruction
- Verification fails repeatedly

**Ask for clarification rather than guessing.**

## When to Revisit Earlier Steps

**Return to Review (Step 1) when:**
- Partner updates the plan based on your feedback
- Fundamental approach needs rethinking

**Don't force through blockers** - stop and ask.

## Remember
- Review plan critically first
- Follow plan steps exactly
- Don't skip verifications
- Reference skills when plan says to
- Stop when blocked, don't guess
- Never start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent

Base directory for this skill: /Users/buemura/.claude/plugins/cache/superpowers-dev/superpowers/6.3.0/skills/finishing-a-development-branch

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Detect environment → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## Step 1: Verify Tests

Run the project's full test suite (`npm test` / `cargo test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...`).

**If tests fail**, report the failures and stop — the menu comes after a green suite:

```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]
```

**If tests pass:** continue to Step 2.

## Step 2: Detect Environment

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
# Capture now, while still inside the workspace — Step 5 changes directory
# before cleanup (Step 6) needs this value
WORKTREE_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

This determines which menu to show and how cleanup works:

| State | Menu | Cleanup |
|-------|------|---------|
| `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (normal repo) | Standard 3 options | No worktree to clean up |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, named branch | Standard 3 options | Provenance-based (see Step 6) |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, detached HEAD | Reduced 2 options (no merge) | Externally managed — leave in place |

## Step 3: Determine Base Branch

The base branch is whatever this work forked from — usually named in the
plan, the conversation, or the branch's upstream. If it is not already
known, ask: "This branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?"
Confirm before merging: merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo.

## Step 4: Present Options

**Normal repo and named-branch worktree — present exactly these 3 options:**

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

**Detached HEAD — present exactly these 2 options:**

```
Implementation complete. You're on a detached HEAD (externally managed workspace).

1. Push as new branch and create a Pull Request
2. Keep as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

Present the menu exactly as written — concise, with every option coming
from the list above. Discarding the work happens only in response to your
human partner explicitly asking for it (see "If your human partner asks to
discard the work" below). Wait for their answer; the integration decision
is theirs.

## Step 5: Execute Choice

### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Get main repo root for CWD safety
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"

# Merge first — verify success before removing anything
git checkout <base-branch>
git pull
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>
```

If tests fail on the merged result: stop, leave the worktree and branch in
place, and investigate — nothing has been pushed, so the merge is local
and recoverable.

Once the merged result is green: clean up the worktree (Step 6), then
delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
git push -u origin <feature-branch>
# From a detached HEAD, name the new branch on the remote:
# git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch>
```

Then create the pull/merge request against <base-branch> with the forge's
tooling — its CLI if one is available, or the creation URL most forges
print when you push — following the repo's PR template and conventions if
present, and report the URL to your human partner.

Keep the worktree — your human partner iterates on PR feedback there.

### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

### If your human partner asks to discard the work

This path exists only as a response to an explicit request to throw the
work away. Confirm first:

```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for that exact confirmation. When it arrives:

```bash
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"
```

Then clean up the worktree (Step 6) and force-delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -D <feature-branch>
```

## Step 6: Cleanup Workspace

**Runs for Option 1 and confirmed discards.** Options 2 and 3 always
preserve the worktree. Both callers have already changed directory to the
main repo root — worktree removal must run from outside the worktree —
and use the `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON`/`WORKTREE_PATH` values captured in
Step 2, from before that directory change.

**If `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON`:** Normal repo, no worktree to clean up. Done.

**If `WORKTREE_PATH` is under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`:** Superpowers
created this worktree — we own cleanup:

```bash
git worktree remove "$WORKTREE_PATH"
git worktree prune  # Self-healing: clean up any stale registrations
```

**If removal is refused** (`contains modified or untracked files`): the
worktree holds files that exist nowhere else — uncommitted plans, notes,
or scratch work. Never `--force` on your own initiative. Show your human
partner what is at stake and ask:

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" status --porcelain -uall
```

```
Worktree removal refused — these files were never committed:

<file list>

1. Commit them to <branch> before cleanup
2. Move them into <main repo root>
3. Delete them (unrecoverable)

Which?
```

Carry out the choice, then remove the worktree.

**Otherwise:** The host environment owns this workspace — leave it in
place. If your platform provides a workspace-exit tool, use it.

## Quick Reference

| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
| 1. Merge locally | yes | - | - | yes |
| 2. Create PR | - | yes | yes | - |
| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | yes | - |
| Discard (explicit request only) | - | - | - | yes (force) |

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Tests passed earlier this session" | Run the suite on the tree you are about to integrate. A green run only proves the tree it ran on. |
| "They obviously want it merged" | Integration is your human partner's decision. Present the menu and wait. |
| "They seem done with this feature — I'll offer to discard it" | The menu is complete as written. Discard happens only when your human partner asks for it in so many words. |
| "'Yeah, get rid of it' counts as confirmation" | Only the typed word `discard` authorizes deletion. |
| "The PR is up, so the worktree is clutter now" | PR feedback gets fixed in that worktree. It stays until the work lands. |
| "This other worktree looks stale — I'll clean it too" | Clean up only worktrees under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`. Everything else belongs to the host. |
| "Removal refused — `--force` is just finishing the cleanup" | The refusal means files exist only in that worktree. `--force` destroys them permanently. Show your human partner and ask. |
| "The merged-result failure is probably flaky" | A failing merged result stops everything. Branch and worktree stay put while you investigate. |
| "The base branch is obviously main" | Confirm the fork point or ask. Merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo. |
| "The push was rejected — force-push will fix it" | A rejected push means the remote moved. Investigate; force-push only on your human partner's explicit request. |

1	# Phase 2 — Editor Core Implementation Plan
2	
3	> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
4	
5	**Goal:** A working Markdown editor with no AI yet: three tabs (Editor / Preview / AI Review placeholder), a CodeMirror 6 editor, a rendered preview, autosave to localStorage, export to a `.md` file, and a light/dark theme toggle.
6	
7	**Architecture:** All state lives in React context providers (`ThemeProvider`, `DocumentProvider`). Pure helpers (`storage`, `theme`, `exportFilename`) carry the logic and are unit-tested on their own. The editor is a thin React wrapper around a CodeMirror `EditorView` that is created once. Props are synced into the view through `Compartment`s and minimal change transactions. All tab panels stay mounted, and inactive ones are only hidden, so the editor keeps its undo history and cursor when the user switches tabs.
8	
9	**Tech Stack:** React 19, TypeScript (strict), Vite, Tailwind CSS v4 (+ `@tailwindcss/typography`), Zod v4, CodeMirror 6, `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm`, Vitest + Testing Library + jsdom.
10	
11	**Spec:** [docs/specs/00-overview.md](00-overview.md). Read the "Frontend contract" section before starting. Names and signatures below are copied from it.
12	
13	## Global Constraints
14	
15	- Node 24, pnpm. Run all frontend commands from the repo root with `pnpm --dir web …`.
16	- TypeScript strict. No `any`.
17	- localStorage keys: `ai-docs:document` → `{ content: string; updatedAt: number }`, `ai-docs:theme` → `"light" | "dark"`. Every read is validated with Zod and never throws.
18	- Theme defaults to `light`. Dark mode adds the class `dark` on `document.documentElement` (Tailwind v4 class-based dark variant, set up in phase 1).
19	- Document autosave is debounced by **300 ms**.
20	- Export filename: slug of the first `# ` heading + `.md`, otherwise `document.md`.
21	- `TextRange = { from: number; to: number }` uses UTF-16 offsets, with `from <= to`.
22	- `TabId = 'editor' | 'preview' | 'review'`. Tab labels: `Editor`, `Preview`, `AI Review`.
23	- All interactive controls are keyboard-reachable and have accessible names. Tests query by role and name.
24	- TDD on every task: failing test → minimal implementation → passing test → commit (Conventional Commits).
25	- No network calls in this phase.
26

29	- `web/` exists with Vite + React 19 + TS, and the scripts `lint`, `typecheck`, `test` (`vitest run`), `build`, `dev`.

211	export function loadJson<T>(key: string, schema: z.ZodType<T>, fallback: T): T {
212	  try {
213	    const raw = window.localStorage.getItem(key)
214	    if (raw === null) return fallback
215	    const parsed = schema.safeParse(JSON.parse(raw))
216	    return parsed.success ? parsed.data : fallback
217	  } catch {
218	    return fallback
219	  }
220	}

223	  try {

228	  }
229	}

234	export function downloadTextFile(
235	  filename: string,
236	  text: string,
237	  mime = 'text/markdown;charset=utf-8',
238	): void {
239	  const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([text], { type: mime }))
240	  const anchor = document.createElement('a')
241	  anchor.href = url
242	  anchor.download = filename
243	  anchor.style.display = 'none'
244	  document.body.appendChild(anchor)
245	  anchor.click()
246	  anchor.remove()
247	  // Revoke on the next tick so the browser has started the download.
248	  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 0)
249	}

806	import {
807	  createContext,
808	  useContext,
809	  useEffect,
810	  useMemo,
811	  useReducer,
812	  useRef,
813	  type ReactNode,
814	} from 'react'
815	import { loadJson, saveJson } from '../../lib/storage'
816	import { initialContent } from './initialContent'
817	import { DOCUMENT_STORAGE_KEY, storedDocumentSchema, type TextRange } from './schema'
818	
819	export type DocumentContextValue = {
820	  content: string
821	  selection: TextRange
822	  setContent(content: string): void
823	  setSelection(range: TextRange): void
824	  replaceRange(range: TextRange, text: string): void
825	}
826	
827	type State = { content: string; selection: TextRange }
828	
829	type Action =
830	  | { type: 'setContent'; content: string }
831	  | { type: 'setSelection'; range: TextRange }
832	  | { type: 'replaceRange'; range: TextRange; text: string }
833	
834	const AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS = 300
835	
836	function clampRange(range: TextRange, length: number): TextRange {
837	  const a = Math.min(Math.max(range.from, 0), length)
838	  const b = Math.min(Math.max(range.to, 0), length)
839	  return { from: Math.min(a, b), to: Math.max(a, b) }
840	}
841	
842	function reducer(state: State, action: Action): State {
843	  switch (action.type) {
844	    case 'setContent':
845	      return {
846	        content: action.content,
847	        selection: clampRange(state.selection, action.content.length),
848	      }
849	    case 'setSelection':
850	      return { ...state, selection: clampRange(action.range, state.content.length) }
851	    case 'replaceRange': {
852	      const { from, to } = clampRange(action.range, state.content.length)
853	      const content = state.content.slice(0, from) + action.text + state.content.slice(to)
854	      const cursor = from + action.text.length
855	      return { content, selection: { from: cursor, to: cursor } }
856	    }
857	  }
858	}
859	
860	function loadInitialState(): State {
861	  const stored = loadJson(DOCUMENT_STORAGE_KEY, storedDocumentSchema.nullable(), null)
862	  return { content: stored?.content ?? initialContent, selection: { from: 0, to: 0 } }
863	}
864	
865	function persist(content: string): void {
866	  saveJson(DOCUMENT_STORAGE_KEY, { content, updatedAt: Date.now() })
867	}
868	
869	const DocumentContext = createContext<DocumentContextValue | null>(null)
870	
871	export function DocumentProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
872	  const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, undefined, loadInitialState)
873	  const latestContent = useRef(state.content)
874	  const hasUnsavedChange = useRef(false)
875	
876	  useEffect(() => {
877	    latestContent.current = state.content
878	    hasUnsavedChange.current = true
879	    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
880	      persist(state.content)
881	      hasUnsavedChange.current = false
882	    }, AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS)
883	    return () => clearTimeout(timer)
884	  }, [state.content])
885	
886	  useEffect(() => {
887	    const flush = () => {
888	      if (!hasUnsavedChange.current) return
889	      persist(latestContent.current)
890	      hasUnsavedChange.current = false
891	    }
892	    window.addEventListener('pagehide', flush)
893	    return () => window.removeEventListener('pagehide', flush)
894	  }, [])
895	
896	  const value = useMemo<DocumentContextValue>(
897	    () => ({
898	      content: state.content,
899	      selection: state.selection,
900	      setContent: (content) => dispatch({ type: 'setContent', content }),
901	      setSelection: (range) => dispatch({ type: 'setSelection', range }),
902	      replaceRange: (range, text) => dispatch({ type: 'replaceRange', range, text }),
903	    }),
904	    [state],
905	  )
906	
907	  return <DocumentContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</DocumentContext.Provider>
908	}
909	
910	// eslint-disable-next-line react-refresh/only-export-components -- hook is colocated with its provider
911	export function useDocument(): DocumentContextValue {
912	  const value = useContext(DocumentContext)
913	  if (!value) throw new Error('useDocument must be used inside <DocumentProvider>')
914	  return value
915	}
916	```

1197	function minimalChange(current: string, next: string) {
1198	  const max = Math.min(current.length, next.length)
1199	  let start = 0

1204	    endCurrent--
1205	    endNext--
1206	  }
